instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines "lobbyist" as anyone who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" to lobby — any amount of economic consideration triggers lobbyist status, with no dollar threshold.

The statutory definition of "lobbyist" in §13.62(11) is based on receipt of economic consideration and lobbying duties, not on any expenditure-amount threshold by the lobbyist; no lobbyist-side expenditure trigger is defined.

§13.68(1)(a)5 provides that expenditures for paid advertising and public-grassroots activities are included in the aggregate only if total such expenditures exceed $500 in the reporting period, establishing a de minimis disclosure threshold (Tier −1).

§13.621(5) allows a principal anticipating no more than $500 in aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year to file a verified statement and be exempt from licensing, registration, and reporting; §13.64(1) correspondingly requires registration only after expenditures exceed $500.

No percentage-of-time exemption for lobbyist filing exists in the statute; §13.62(11) uses a day-count test (5 days), and §13.68(1)(a)'s 10-hour carve-out applies to a principal's aggregate reporting of non-lobbyist employees, not a percent-of-time exemption from a lobbyist's own filing duty.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell against the Wisconsin statute text.

**row_001**: §13.62(11) defines "Lobbyist" as one who "is employed by a principal, or contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" — no dollar threshold; any economic consideration triggers it.

**row_002**: No expenditure-based threshold for lobbyist definition exists; the $500 threshold in §13.64 is for principal registration, not lobbyist definition.

**row_003**: §13.62(11) — "If an individual's duties on behalf of a principal are not limited exclusively to lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period." This is a day-based time standard.

**row_004**: §13.68(1)(a)5 — paid advertising/public-urging expenditures included only "if the total amount...exceeds $500 during the reporting period"; §13.68(1)(a)6 — itemize lobbyist payments only if exceeding $200. There is a de minimis reporting threshold.

**row_005**: §13.621(5) — principals with aggregate expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and are exempt from registration/reporting.

**row_006**: No percentage-of-time exemption for lobbyist filing exists in the statute. §13.68(1)(a) excludes employees who devote ≤10 hours to lobbying from the principal's aggregate reporting, but that's hours-based, not a percent, and it's for principal reporting, not lobbyist filing exemption.

§13.62(11) provides that if an individual's duties are not exclusively lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period.

§13.621(5) allows a principal anticipating no more than $500 in aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year to file a verified statement and be exempt from licensing, registration, and reporting; §13.64(1) correspondingly requires registration only after expenditures exceed $500.

No percentage-of-time exemption for lobbyist filing exists in the statute; §13.62(11) uses a day-count test (5 days), and §13.68(1)(a)'s 10-hour carve-out applies to a principal's aggregate reporting of non-lobbyist employees, not a percent-of-time exemption from a lobbyist's own filing duty.
